forest_complement.statement: (Lemma 5.1.3) Let $f$ be a measurable function with $\|f(x)\| \le \mathbf{1}_F(x)$ for all $x \in X$. Then the integral over $G \setminus G'$ of the Carleson sum over the tiles not in $\mathfrak{P}_1$ satisfies $$\int_{G\setminus G'} \Big\|\sum_{p \in \mathfrak{P}_1^c} T_p f(x)\Big\|\,dx \le C_{5.1.3}(a, q)\, \mu(G)^{1-1/q}\, \mu(F)^{1/q},$$ where $q$ is the exponent `nnq X` and $C_{5.1.3}(a,q)$ is the constant `C5_1_3`.
forest_complement.sketch: It follows from the optimized version `forest_complement_optimized`, whose constant $C_{5.1.3}^{\mathrm{opt}}(a,q)$ is bounded above by $C_{5.1.3}(a,q)$.

𝔓pos.statement: The set $\mathfrak{P}_{G\setminus G'}$ of the blueprint: a distinguished subset of the tiles $\mathfrak{P}(X)$ (`𝔓pos`).

lintegral_carlesonSum_𝔓₁_compl_le_sum_li.statement: Let $f$ be measurable. Then $\int_{G\setminus G'} \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_1^c, f)(x)\|\,dx$ is at most the sum of the following four terms, where every integral is over $G \setminus G'$ and $\mathfrak{P}_{pos}$ denotes `𝔓pos`: (i) $\sum_{n \le \mathrm{max}\mathfrak{C}} \sum_{k \le n} \sum_{l < n} \int \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{L}_0'(k,n,l), f)(x)\|\,dx$; (ii) $\sum_{n \le \mathrm{max}\mathfrak{C}} \sum_{k \le n} \sum_{j \le 2n+3} \sum_{l \le Z(n+1)} \int \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{L}_1(k,n,j,l), f)(x)\|\,dx$; (iii) $\sum_{n \le \mathrm{max}\mathfrak{C}} \sum_{k \le n} \sum_{j \le 2n+3} \int \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{L}_2(k,n,j), f)(x)\|\,dx$; (iv) $\sum_{n \le \mathrm{max}\mathfrak{C}} \sum_{k \le n} \sum_{j \le 2n+3} \sum_{l \le Z(n+1)} \int \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{L}_3(k,n,j,l), f)(x)\|\,dx$. Here $\mathrm{max}\mathfrak{C}$ is `maxℭ X` and $Z$ is `defaultZ a`. The sets on the right-hand side are, by design, antichains.
lintegral_carlesonSum_𝔓₁_compl_le_sum_li.sketch: Putting together the previous decomposition lemmas: the tiles of $\mathfrak{P}_1^c$ relevant on $G\setminus G'$ are split, using the sets $\mathfrak{C}(k,n)$, $\mathfrak{B}(k,n,p)$, densities `dens'` and the sets $E$, $E_2$, into the families $\mathfrak{L}_0'$, $\mathfrak{L}_1$, $\mathfrak{L}_2$, $\mathfrak{L}_3$, and the triangle inequality for the Carleson sum then gives the bound.

lintegral_enorm_carlesonSum_le_of_isAnti.statement: Let $f$ be measurable with $\|f(x)\| \le \mathbf{1}_F(x)$ for all $x$, and let $\mathfrak{A}$ be an antichain (for $\le$ on tiles) with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{C}(k,n)$. Then $$\int_{G\setminus G'} \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{A}, f)(x)\|\,dx \le C_{2.0.3}(a,q)\, 2^{a+3}\, \mu(G)^{1-1/q}\, \mu(F)^{1/q}\, 2^{-\frac{q-1}{8a^4} n},$$ where $\mathfrak{P}_{pos}$ is `𝔓pos` and $q$ is `nnq X`.
lintegral_enorm_carlesonSum_le_of_isAnti.sketch: Apply the antichain operator estimate `antichain_operator_le_volume` to the antichain $\mathfrak{P}_{pos} \cap \mathfrak{P}_1^c \cap \mathfrak{A}$ on $G\setminus G'$, and bound its density $\mathrm{dens}_1$ using that the tiles lie in $\mathfrak{C}(k,n)$ (controlling `dens'` and the enlarged tiles $\lambda p$ via the sets $E_2$, $\mathfrak{C}_2$, $\mathfrak{U}_1$), which produces the factors $2^{a+3}$ and $2^{-\frac{q-1}{8a^4}n}$.

forest_complement_optimized.statement: Let $f$ be measurable with $\|f(x)\| \le \mathbf{1}_F(x)$ for all $x \in X$. Then $$\int_{G\setminus G'} \|\mathrm{carlesonSum}(\mathfrak{P}_1^c, f)(x)\|\,dx \le C^{\mathrm{opt}}_{5.1.3}(a, q)\, \mu(G)^{1-1/q}\, \mu(F)^{1/q},$$ where $C^{\mathrm{opt}}_{5.1.3}$ is the constant `C5_1_3_optimized` and $q$ is `nnq X`.
forest_complement_optimized.sketch: Decompose using `lintegral_carlesonSum_𝔓₁_compl_le_sum_lintegral`, bound each of the resulting antichain terms by `lintegral_enorm_carlesonSum_le_of_isAntichain_subset_ℭ` (each family lies in some $\mathfrak{C}(k,n)$), and sum the geometric factors $2^{-\frac{q-1}{8a^4}n}$ over the index ranges to obtain the constant.
